doc-title: Make your own | AI Skill Trees
meta-description: Build a skill tree for your own subject. Your spreadsheet stays on your machine; you get back one HTML file that works offline.
page-lede: A skill tree is one spreadsheet. Make it with an AI chat, open it here, change anything you disagree with on screen, and download it as one HTML file for your students. No account, no installation, no cost.
start-drop: Drop tree.csv or a downloaded tree (.html) here, or click to choose
start-catalogue: Find a tree in the catalogue
picker-heading: Start from a tree in the catalogue
picker-load-error: Could not load the catalogue. Try again, or start another way.
search-placeholder: Subject, level, topic or keyword — e.g. “2P”, “statistics”, “growth factor”
empty-body: Try fewer filters or a broader search.
start-catalogue-hint: You get your own copy to change. The published tree is not affected.
start-no-tree: That was not a tree. Choose a tree.csv, or an .html file downloaded from this site.
paste-placeholder: Paste the spreadsheet the chat gave you here (Ctrl+V or ⌘V)
paste-not-tree: That does not look like a skill tree. Copy the whole spreadsheet from the chat, from the line that starts with id,type,topic down to the last row.
start-html-bad: {name} does not contain a skill tree. Only files downloaded from this site can be opened here.
start-fetch-failed: The tree could not be fetched. Check your connection and try again.
split-label: Panel width. Drag, or use the arrow keys
copy-errors: Copy the list for your AI chat
copy-preamble: The skill tree builder found these problems in the tree.csv you made for me. Please fix them and give me the whole corrected file back.
node-resources-hint: Exam tasks, textbook sections, videos. The student sees them under the node, and in “Resources” in the tree's menu. Click one to change it.
res-count: {n} of the tree's {total} resources. Click one to add it to this node.
res-none-in-tree: The tree has no resources yet. Make the first one with “New resource”.
res-no-match: No resource matches. Make it with “New resource”.
res-all-attached: The node already has every resource in the tree.
res-group-hint: The heading it is listed under, e.g. “Exam” or “Textbook”. Pick one the tree already uses, or write a new one.
res-url-hint: Optional. Without a link, the title is shown as text, e.g. “2026 Spring, Part 1, task 3”.
res-edit-shared: This resource belongs to {n} nodes ({names}). A change here changes it on all of them.
res-need-label: Write a title or a link.
res-duplicate: Another resource has the same title and link. Add that one to the nodes instead.
res-confirm-delete: “{name}” belongs to no other node. Delete the resource from the tree?
download-note: The spreadsheet is what you keep and edit. The tree is one HTML file for your students: it opens by double-clicking and works offline.
err-render: The tree could not be drawn: {message}
err-timeout: The tree did not finish drawing. That usually means the file is not a skill tree spreadsheet at all.
confirm-discard: You have changes that are not downloaded. Open another tree anyway?
blank-node-description: Term: what it means, in one sentence.
view-intro: This is the tree as your students will see it. Click a node to see the instruction it gives them.
tree-intro: Click a node in the tree, or in the list, to edit it.
node-none: Click a node in the tree to edit it.
topic-delete: Delete the topic and all its nodes
confirm-delete-topic: Delete the topic “{topic}” and all {n} nodes in it? You can undo it with Undo.
node-type-hint: A skill is something the student does. A concept is something the student has to understand and explain. Facts are a list the student has to know by heart.
node-description-skill: What the student can do, finishing the sentence “The student can …”.
node-description-concept: The term and its definition, as “Term: definition”. One per line if the node holds several.
node-description-fact: What the student can recall, one item per line as “cue: answer” (“the year Norway joined NATO: 1949”, “perro: dog”). A line with no colon is a rule the items are made from.
node-prereqs-none: Nothing: the student can start here.
node-prereqs-hint: Only the nearest prerequisites. The tutor finds the rest by following the arrows.
node-pick-hint: Click nodes in the tree to add or remove them as prerequisites. Dashed outline: this node builds on it.
node-cycle: “{dep}” already builds on “{node}”, so it cannot also be a prerequisite for it. That would be a circle.
node-aids-hint: Which of the tree’s aid levels this node is examined under. Set the levels under Tree.
node-instruction-hint: Added to the tutor’s instruction for this node only. Leave empty if the general instruction is enough.
node-id-hint: The node’s key in the spreadsheet. Changing it updates every arrow, but students who already have the file lose their tick on this node.
node-id-taken: Another node already has the id “{id}”.
instr-loading: The instructions appear when the tree has been built.
instr-intro: These are the instructions your students paste into their AI chat. Each one is in a few parts; open a part with Edit to see all its text and change it for this tree only. The rest stays as published, and your version is saved as a row in the spreadsheet. Every instruction ends with Extra, for anything you want to add. Words in {braces} are filled in by the tree.
cond-courseSpecifics: When the tree has a course text
motNoStart: When the student has not said where they are
motStartHard: When the student finds it hard
motStartBored: When the student finds it boring
motStartUse: When the student asks what it is for
miniThreeLevels: When each goal has three levels
miniOneLevel: When each goal has one level
miniMixedTest: When the file ends with a mixed test
miniGame: When the file has game elements
miniEasyRead: When the text is easy to read
miniReadAloud: When the text can be read aloud
simDesignFirst: When the design is agreed first
simBuildNow: When the simulation is built straight away
simTasks: When the simulation comes with tasks
simCritique: When the students criticise the model
cond-lessonIntro: When the lesson type is Introduction
cond-lessonPractice: When the lesson type is Practice
cond-lessonReview: When the lesson type is Review
cond-lessonOther: When the lesson type is Other
grp-how: Change any text and press Save. A row you have changed is marked green; “Use the published text” takes it back. Empty a row to leave that section out of this tree’s instruction.
sec-extra-placeholder: Anything else you want the AI to know or do. Left empty, nothing is added.
sec-apply-all: Use this text in every instruction that has this section ({list})
sec-runtime-node: Written on each node, under “Extra instruction for this node”.
sec-runtime-aids: Written from the aid levels under Tree.
set-learner-hint: In the definite form, as the instructions say it: “the student”, “the participant”. Empty gives the language’s default.
set-family-hint: Adds what the instructions should know about this kind of subject.
set-decomposition-hint: Which version of the method the tree was built with, so you can tell later.
set-group-course-note: Shown to students under “About the subject”.
set-subtitle-hint: One line under the title on the tree’s card, e.g. “Programme subject, Year 12”.
set-group-catalogue-note: What the filters on aiskilltrees.com/trees/ sort by. Also shown under “About the subject”.
set-keywords-hint: Extra words the catalogue search should find the tree by, separated by semicolons.
set-author-inherited: This tree was made by {author}. If you are adapting it, write your own name here: {author} is then listed under “Based on”, as the CC BY licence requires. Leave the field empty if you are {author}.
set-based-on-hint: The trees this one was made from, nearest first. Shown to students under “About the subject”, and kept in the file when it is downloaded.
set-motivation-hint: A button that starts a conversation about why the subject is worth learning.
set-group-slots-note: Filled into the instructions wherever they refer to the course.
set-slot-course: Course name, as the instructions say it
set-slot-motivation: The subject, in the motivation dialogue
set-slot-expression: What students often get wrong in writing
set-slot-expression-hint: The tutor watches for this in every answer.
set-slot-specifics-hint: Anything every instruction should know: the level, the textbook, what the students have done before.
set-group-aids-note: For subjects that are examined with and without aids. Leave empty if yours is not.
set-aids-label-hint: For example “Part”, so the tags read “Part 1” and “Part 2”.
set-aids-new-student: Describe the aids the student may use.
set-aids-new-model: Describe the aids the student may use, so the AI can set tasks that fit.
set-group-other-note: Settings this page has no field for, shown as they stand in the spreadsheet.
set-add-prompt: Name of the setting (as in the name column):
look-intro: The colour of each type of node, and the font. The type is always written on the node too, so the colour never has to carry the meaning alone.
look-contrast: The node names will be hard to read on this colour (contrast {ratio}:1, 4.5:1 is the minimum). Try a lighter or less saturated colour.
look-font-hint: These fonts are on every computer already, so the downloaded tree looks the same without a network.
l0-body: Copy the instruction below into whichever AI chat you already use. It asks about your subject, your level and your curriculum, takes you through the decomposition, and hands you a spreadsheet at the end. Nothing to install.
l1-cta-note: Nine nodes, two resources, and every setting a tree can have. It is also the best thing to hand the AI as a format example.
l2-title: You are going to live with this
l2-body: If you will maintain a tree over several years, or build them for a whole department, it is worth working in an editor with an AI agent that can read the specification, run the checks and keep your versions. The method repository has the decomposition model, the default instructions and the file format.
contribute-body: Made a tree you want other teachers to use? You can submit it to the catalogue on this site.
stat-roots-flat: That is a lot. A tree where most nodes start from nothing is usually one where the prerequisites were never worked out — worth sending back to the AI.
set-decomposition-missing: not given — add a decompositionVersion row, so you can tell later which version of the method the tree was built with
l1-body: Drop it here, or paste it if you copied it from the chat. A tree you downloaded from this site earlier works too. It opens in the editor, where you can change it and download it again.
l0-next: Copied. Paste it into your AI chat. When the chat gives you the spreadsheet, drop it in the box next to this one, or copy it and paste it there.
l3-title: You want to start from something
ov-close: Close and look at the example
ov-foot-l2: Maintaining trees for years, or for a whole department? Work in an editor with an AI agent instead:
ov-foot-contribute: Made a tree other teachers could use?
rep-settings-note: Some of these you wrote, and some were worked out from your file. A tree that looks wrong is usually one of these.
privacy-note: Nothing is uploaded, and nothing is saved in your browser. Your tree exists only on this page until you download it.
footer-affiliation: Part of a research project at KURT – Centre for Teaching and Learning in Science, University of Oslo.
status-flat: No errors, but most nodes have no prerequisites. See View.
grp-lessonPlan-role-and-style: Who the AI is, how the answer is laid out, and the language it is written in.
grp-lessonPlan-the-lesson: The learning goals and the plan for the lesson, one for each type of lesson the teacher can choose: introduction, practice, review or other. Plus how skill, concept and fact goals are taught.
grp-lessonPlan-context: What the students already know, the aids they may use, and anything particular to the course.
grp-lessonPlan-extra: Your own additions. Empty unless you write something here.
grp-motivation-role-and-style: Who the AI is, its warmth, one question at a time, how it opens, and the language it writes in.
grp-motivation-the-conversation: The core message, getting to know the student, their strengths, and where the conversation is heading.
grp-motivation-arguments: The arguments for practising now and for the long term.
grp-motivation-context: Anything particular to the course, and that the AI remembers nothing between chats.
grp-motivation-extra: Your own additions. Empty unless you write something here.
grp-node-role-and-style: Who the AI is, how it opens the conversation, its tone, how long its messages are, and the language it writes in.
grp-node-how-to-teach: How the AI leads into the topic, uses examples and analogies, and adjusts the difficulty.
grp-node-the-goal: What the student is to master on this node, for skills, concepts and facts, and when it counts as mastered.
grp-node-context: What the student already knows, the aids allowed, anything particular to the course, and that the AI remembers nothing between chats.
grp-node-extra: Your own additions. Empty unless you write something here.
grp-exam-role-and-style: Who the AI is and the language it writes in.
grp-exam-the-test: Which goals the test covers, what the tasks look like, and that answers are held back until the student has tried.
grp-exam-skills-concepts-and-facts: How tasks are mixed when the test covers concepts and facts as well as skills.
grp-exam-context: The aids allowed, anything particular to the course, and that the AI remembers nothing between chats.
grp-exam-extra: Your own additions. Empty unless you write something here.
